newsitem.title: MONTSERRAT: Volcano island Montserrat denies plans to evacuate.
newsitem.headline: Volcano island Montserrat denies plans to evacuate.

text.p: The government of Montserrat, the tiny British colony that is the site of an active volcano, denied on Thursday that it was planning an imminent, island-wide evacuation.
"Nothing could be further from the truth," said Howard Fergus, the island's acting governor, in a radio address to the nation that aired on Thursday morning.

He said there were two officers from the British Army's Irish Guards and a senior police officer from the Kent Constabulary in England on the island working on an evacuation plan, but it was to be used only if volcanic activity increased.

"It is only prudent and good common sense to have contingency plans in place," Fergus said. He also noted that there had been such a long-term evacuation plan in place for two years and that it currently was being fine tuned.
Montserrat's population has slipped from about 11,000 to 6,800 since July 1995, when the island's volcano roared to life after centuries of virtual dormancy.

Island residents remaining have been confined for more than a year to the northern section of the island, which scientists believe would be safe from a violent eruption because it is protected by a range of mountains.
